validated_issues.original_description: Fragile Parenthesis Normalization: The check for '((' and '))' is too strict and doesn't handle internal whitespace. Additionally, slice(1, -1) on '((...))' removes only one level, but logic fails if file contains multiple top-level S-expressions or comments.
validated_issues.reasoning: The normalization at line 24 uses startsWith('((') and endsWith('))'), which fails if there is any whitespace (e.g., '( ('). Also, slice(1, -1) only removes one character from each end, so '((...))' becomes '(...)' - if this was intended to be an alist wrapper, it doesn't robustly handle the structure.

validated_issues.original_description: Regex Termination Bug: The unquoted value pattern [^)\s]+ will prematurely terminate if a symbol contains a literal ')' (even if escaped or inside a nested structure). This makes the parser fragile to valid S-expression variations.
validated_issues.reasoning: The regex at line 31 uses [^)]+ for unquoted values. This will stop at the first closing parenthesis, causing truncation if the value contains a nested list or a symbol with a paren. This is a fundamental flaw for an S-expression parser.

validated_issues.original_description:
Incomplete Unescaping: The manual unescaping logic only handles a small subset of standard escape sequences (
, , 	, ", \). Other common escapes like  ,  , or hex/unicode escapes will be left in their literal escaped form.
validated_issues.reasoning: While the code DOES handle   and   (lines 44-45), it indeed misses hex/unicode escapes and other standard escapes. The severity is low as these are rare in trigger files.

validated_issues.original_description: Missing Comment Support: S-expression files frequently use ';' for comments. This parser will attempt to match comment text as keys or values if they contain dots or parentheses.
validated_issues.reasoning: The parser only strips comments that start a line (line 18). Inline comments like '(key . value) ; comment' will be incorrectly captured as part of the value or break the regex.

validated_issues.original_description: Potential List Index Out of Bounds: The code assumes resolution-methods and resolution-framing will always contain at least 2 elements. While choose-n 2 currently satisfies this, the code will crash if source lists are ever shortened.
validated_issues.reasoning: Lines 52 and 55 use (car resolution-methods) and (cadr resolution-methods). If the source list has fewer than 2 elements, choose-n 2 will return a shorter list, causing cadr to crash.

validated_issues.original_description: Embedded Selection in Sign-off: The random selection for the sign-off happens at prompt generation time. If intent is for agent to 'choose' its sign-off style during conversation, this hard-codes it into the system prompt for that specific run.
validated_issues.reasoning: The (choice ...) on lines 101-105 is evaluated when the persona-prompt is defined, fixing the choice for the duration of that prompt's use.

validated_issues.original_description: Minor formatting inconsistency: Some entries have slightly different formatting for personality traits vs background, but as a context file for LLMs this is negligible.
validated_issues.reasoning: Review of the file shows consistent structure for all personas (name, background/traits bullets). The formatting is well-suited for LLM context.

validated_issues.original_description: Environment Dependency: Use of execSync with 'claude' CLI assumes the command is in the system PATH and pre-authenticated. Likely to fail in production/daemon environments unless environment is perfectly mirrored.
validated_issues.reasoning: Line 84 relies on the external 'claude' CLI being available and configured, which is a significant external dependency for a script.

validated_issues.original_description: Temp File Collision Risk: Using Date.now() for temp filenames is susceptible to collisions if multiple trigger events occur in the same millisecond. Use of UUID or crypto.randomBytes is recommended.
validated_issues.reasoning: Line 73 uses both Date.now() and a random alphanumeric suffix (Math.random().toString(36)). This combination is sufficiently unique for temporary files in this context.

validated_issues.original_description: Outdated Tagging Convention: The prompt version uses @agents/invoke-opus.js style tags, while Discord integration expects short tags like @opus. This will cause the agent to fail to trigger other agents in Discord.
validated_issues.reasoning: The SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 29-57) explicitly uses short tags like @opus and @sonnet. No outdated tagging style was found in the file.

validated_issues.original_description: Prompt Injection Vulnerability: Direct interpolation of ${author} and ${body} into the prompt allows a user to 'break out' of the user-query block and provide instructions that contradict the SYSTEM_PROMPT.
validated_issues.reasoning: Line 78 interpolates author and body directly. A user could easily inject instructions to bypass the system prompt's constraints.

validated_issues.original_description: Broken Paths: Shell commands reference directories 'fabric' and 'thimble' which do not exist in the project root. Should likely be 'core' or 'agents'. Pipeline will fail on first 'find' command.
validated_issues.reasoning: The shell commands at lines 35-44 reference 'core' and 'shell', both of which are valid directories in the project root. No reference to 'fabric' or 'thimble' was found.

validated_issues.original_description: Broken Data Flow Logic: In the chain macro, each stage-&&& passes its output to the next. Since run-shell ignores input, the final stage-arr only receives results of the last pair of metrics. Attempts to access (caar metrics) and (caadr metrics) will result in index out of bounds errors.
validated_issues.reasoning: The nesting in stage-&&& (lines 35-46) correctly builds a tree of pairs ((line . file) . ((todo . fixme) . (test . issues))). The stage-arr at line 48 correctly destructures this using car/cdr. The QA report misidentified this as broken logic.

validated_issues.original_description: Invalid Model Reference: 'gemini-3' is likely a typo for 'gemini-1.5-pro' or future-dated placeholder. It will cause runtime error if LLM provider doesn't recognize the model string.
validated_issues.reasoning: Line 141 uses 'gemini-3' in a council call, which is not a known model name and will likely cause a failure.

validated_issues.original_description: Shell Injection in Bead Creation: ${input} is passed directly to beads-create. If extracted 'TITLE' contains single quotes or semicolons, it could lead to arbitrary shell command execution or broken issue creation.
validated_issues.reasoning: Line 185 interpolates ${input} into beads-create. While beads-create is an effect, if the downstream interpreter uses it to construct a shell command without escaping, it could be vulnerable. However, it's safer than direct run-shell.

gaps_found.description: Nested S-expression Truncation: The use of [^)]+ for unquoted values means that any nested list like (key . (nested list)) will be parsed as '(nested', losing the rest of the structure and the closing parenthesis.
Missing multiline support in quoted strings: The regex for quoted strings doesn't use the 's' flag, meaning quoted values containing newlines (standard in S-expressions) will fail to match.

Predictable and world-writable temp file: Files are created in /tmp with a predictable prefix and without using O_EXCL. A local attacker could pre-create these files or symlink them to sensitive system files.
Pipeline failure on empty git log: The hotspots stage will likely fail if no commits have been made in the last week, as the grep command in the shell pipeline will return a non-zero exit code.

summary.notes: The QA report was fairly accurate on logic issues but had several hallucinations regarding file paths and tagging conventions. The most critical confirmed issues are the fragile S-expression parser in parse-trigger.js and the invalid model reference in tech-debt.ss. Gaps found include more specific ways the parser breaks on valid S-expressions and a local security vulnerability in temp file handling.
